prompt:
Use the attached image as the reference: the same woman — the personification of Osmium (Os) — seen off duty in her everyday life. Keep her face, eye colour, hair colour, skin tone and body exactly; change only her clothes, pose and place. Do not reuse earlier conversation images.

Output: one vertical 2:3 image, 1024×1536.

Face: exactly the attached image's face — the same short midface and face length-to-width ratio; the camera angle, pose, bangs or a headpiece never make her face look longer or her jaw heavier.

Style: A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance. No flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face or plastic 3D-render finish. Keep this rendering exactly as in the attached image — the same finish, line, shading, skin and colour treatment.

Place: a vaulted wine cellar of her element's kingdom — racks of dusty bottles, a tasting table and candle sconces
Time of day: warm lamplight or candlelight indoors, the rest in shadow.
Outfit: a sommelier look fitted to her body — a short open waistcoat over a strapless corset top, a short skirt, a tasting cup on a chain and ankle boots, showing her shoulders, collarbones and legs as far as the outfit allows, following her curvy figure — a slim waist and rounded hips; intimate areas covered.
POSTURE: standing at a waist-high railing or sill.
COMPOSITION: a waist-up shot of her head, torso and hands; body in side profile, her face in profile too, not turned toward the camera, facing the right of the frame, so her own right side is toward the camera; camera at her eye level.
Lens / perspective: 50mm-equivalent natural perspective with balanced proportions and modest depth compression.
RIGHT HAND: her own right hand is in PROP — her near arm, on the camera side.
LEFT HAND: her own left hand rests on the railing — her far arm, on the side away from the camera.
PROP: with her own right hand she holds a wine glass at chest height; it is all she holds.
GAZE: her eyes rest on what she holds.
EXPRESSION: heavy-lidded eyes, lips slightly parted and relaxed, brow smooth.
Scene note: she is the sommelier nosing a glass before she names the year

Framing: a waist-up shot — the bottom edge crosses her waist; hips, legs and feet are out of frame.

Leave behind everything she wears in the attached image — no crown, tiara, helmet, feathers, headpiece, hairpins from it, armour or regalia; her hair is styled for the everyday outfit, with at most one small accessory.

Her element — osmium: a hard, brittle blue-white metal, the densest natural element at about 22.6 grams per cubic centimetre, twice as heavy as lead and rivalled only by iridium; found in 1803 together with iridium in the black residue left after platinum dissolves in aqua regia, and named from the Greek word for smell because its volatile oxide gives off a sharp, chlorine-like stench; that oxide vapour stains fats black and has long been used to reveal the shapes of cells under the microscope; its hard alloys once tipped fountain-pen nibs and gramophone needles — may show in the outfit's details, motifs or small accessories.

Figure: keep her exact build from the attached image, neither slimmer nor fuller.

Light: the place's own light, lit and coloured the way this style renders light and skin.

One figure in focus, natural hands with five fingers, no text, logo or watermark.
acceptance: user authorized publishing; preserve generated image without regeneration

observations: 1024x1536 confirmed; one adult woman in focus; painted anime finish.
Both arms attached; glass hand near nose and other hand on counter. Background bottle labels contain tiny marks not clearly legible.
